correctness.rationale: For finite Latin affine quandle x▷y=Tx+(I-T)y, T and I-T invertible, all binary term coefficients form exactly R=F_p[T]: the finite set closed under a▷b=Ta+(I-T)b contains 0,I, inverse bijections of right translations, and by conjugating obtains additive translations by every T^j(I-T); those span R. Arbitrary equations have image sum_j c_j V = g(T)V for an ideal generator g dividing the minimal polynomial. Uniform linear fibers yield probability |ker g(T)|/|V|, and each g is realized with a binary equation. Primary module blocks give precisely the claimed p-power levels, with irreducible minimal polynomial iff the spectrum is {p^-n,1}, without assuming a simple module. Our independent closure and rank computation checked explicit examples; all finite dimensions follow from the module argument.

value.rationale: The equational-probability spectrum is a natural finite-algebra invariant already studied by Cardó. The full attainable set for arbitrary Latin Alexander operator—including nilpotent primary blocks, direct sums and a two-variable completeness theorem—is a useful explicit classification. The minimal-spectrum test differs mathematically from simplicity of the module; it is more than a sample calculation.
